question.text: The proportion of independent directors required on the board of an Asset Management Company (AMC) is:

answer.text: At least 50% (half) of the directors must be independent
At least two-thirds of the directors must be independent
At least 75% of the directors must be independent
At least one-third of the directors must be independent

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (p.65) requires that at least 50% of the directors on an AMC's board be independent. This sits inside the broader governance framework that balances management representation with independent oversight at the AMC level. The Trap: The two-thirds independence requirement applies to the Board of Trustees (p.64), not the AMC board. Candidates who remember "two-thirds independent" but lose track of which board it attaches to will pick the wrong answer. Note: Hold the two MF figures in one map — trustees: at least two-thirds independent; AMC directors: at least 50% independent. That is the source-backed contrast the workbook draws.
